mainEntity.name: Are macOS Accessibility permission apps safe?

acceptedAnswer.text: They can be, but the permission is powerful. Grant it only to apps you trust, and prefer tools with clear documentation, active maintenance, and a reason that matches their feature set.

mainEntity.name: Why do Mac utilities ask for Accessibility permission?

acceptedAnswer.text: Window managers, keyboard tools, launchers, and automation utilities may need Accessibility access to observe or control windows, keyboard events, or system UI behavior.
Gojo is a Mac utility that may participate in the Accessibility permission ecosystem for specific workflow features. It is not a replacement for Apple’s built-in assistive technologies.

mainEntity.name: Which Mac utility should I install first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Install the tool that matches the recurring friction. Use Gojo for a notch workspace, Rectangle for snapping, Maccy for clipboard history, AltTab for switching, and Raycast for command-palette workflows.

blocks.label: Short answer
blocks.copy: If you want one broad MacBook notch surface, start with Gojo. If you only need one specialist job, pick the specialist: Rectangle for window snapping, Maccy for clipboard history, AltTab for window switching, f.lux for display warmth, Raycast for keyboard commands, BetterTouchTool for automation, or Karabiner-Elements for keyboard remapping.
points: Best broad workflow: Gojo for media, windows, clipboard, files, calendar, battery, webcam, and display controls in the notch.
Best specialist tools: Rectangle, Maccy, AltTab, f.lux, Raycast, BetterTouchTool, and Karabiner-Elements for focused jobs.
Permission rule: grant Accessibility only when the feature actually needs window, keyboard, or UI control.

blocks.text: How Gojo fits the Accessibility permission space

content.s: Many serious Mac utilities touch the Accessibility permission ecosystem because they need to observe windows, move windows, remap inputs, or automate parts of the interface. Gojo should be evaluated the same way: ask which features need deeper access, whether the request matches the job, and whether the app is transparent about what it changes.
Gojo is strongest when you want a MacBook notch surface for several daily workflows at once. It is not the best answer when you only need one specialist utility with deep configuration.

This roundup is organized by workflow fit, permission scope, and how directly each app solves a Mac utility problem. It favors official product pages and documentation over broad claims, then links each comparison page for deeper context.

items: Official sources checked on July 2, 2026: Rectangle, f.lux, Boring Notch, AltTab, Maccy, Raycast, BetterTouchTool, Karabiner-Elements, and Gojo project pages.
The recommendations are fit-based, not absolute rankings; several tools can run together when their shortcuts and permissions do not conflict.
